The claim that AI language models can pass the US bar examination at above-average scores is true. In a widely cited 2023 study by researchers Daniel Martin Katz, Michael J. Bommarito II, and others, OpenAI's GPT-4 was evaluated on the Uniform Bar Examination (UBE). GPT-4 achieved a score of 297, which comfortably exceeds the passing threshold of 270 required by even the most stringent US jurisdictions (such as New York and California, which requires a 1390/2000, equivalent to a similar high standard). 

While the initial study placed GPT-4 in the 90th percentile (top 10%) of test-takers, a subsequent critique by Eric Martinez (MIT) suggested this comparison was overly optimistic because it compared GPT-4 against the less competitive February exam cohort. Martinez estimated that GPT-4's performance actually falls around the 68th percentile when compared to the more competitive July exam cohort, and around the 48th percentile among only those who passed. However, under both the original and revised analyses, GPT-4's score of 297 remains firmly above the average score of all test-takers (the 50th percentile), and its ability to pass the exam is undisputed. Subsequent models, such as Claude 3 and newer iterations of GPT, have continued to demonstrate comparable or superior capabilities on legal examinations.
title: AI systems now pass the bar exam
